verdict.rationale: Activepieces documents a public, API-key-authenticated REST API with a published OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec (84 paths), which is Platform/Enterprise-only. It also documents a built-in MCP server that lets AI assistants build flows and 'drive the whole platform', so agent-driven flow creation is a first-party capability. However, no evidence shows specific REST endpoints for creating, updating, or publishing a flow; publishing is documented only as a UI button, with an approval gate in Sensitive projects. Missing for 10: documented flow create/update endpoints in the public API, a documented programmatic publish/activate operation, and hands-on corroboration of an agent completing the lifecycle via the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create, update, and activate a workflow programmatically through the public API

citations.quote: Activepieces publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document (84 paths, server https://cloud.activepieces.com/api)
you can pass the API key as a Bearer token in the header
Activepieces includes a built-in MCP server that lets AI assistants build flows, manage tables, test automations, and more
Connect Claude, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client and it drives the whole platform.
